name: AD8655 / AD8656 (ADI low-noise precision CMOS, rail-to-rail, 5 V)
tagline: Low-noise (2.7 nV/√Hz) rail-to-rail CMOS op-amp for 2.7–5.5 V. Builders of portable and USB-powered headphone amps use it where ±15 V parts can't run.
technology: Single-supply CMOS (2.7–5.5 V), rail-to-rail input and output, unity-gain stable. Offset is trimmed with ADI DigiTrim. ADI PCN 23_0068 places the AD8656 among its '0.6 µm CMOS amplifier products' built at TSMC Fab 9/2A/2B, with ADI Limerick added as an alternate wafer fab from 2023. Datasheet figures: 2.7 nV/√Hz at 10 kHz, 28 MHz bandwidth, 220 mA output current. Distributor listings give about 1 pA bias current.

reputation.summary: The part has a niche following among builders of portable and low-voltage (5 V / USB-powered) headphone amps. Head-Fi posters call it a 'nifty low-voltage rail-to-rail dual' that 'sounds quite nice driving headphones directly'. In AD8656-vs-AD8620 threads on Head-Fi and diyAudio, posters rate it below the AD8620 when other things are equal. It is not an 'op-amp rolling' legend in ±15 V gear.
sonic_descriptors: 'sounds quite nice driving headphones directly' (Head-Fi forum post)
typical_uses: USB-bus-powered / single 5 V audio stages (DAC output buffers, headphone drivers)
Low-voltage preamp and buffer stages that need rail-to-rail swing
caveats: Absolute maximum supply is about 5.5 V (2.7–5.5 V operating), so it will be destroyed in a ±12 V/±15 V op-amp socket.
Sold only in surface-mount packages (MSOP-8 and SOIC-8 per the datasheet summary). Rolling it into DIP-8 sockets needs an adapter.
Forum comparisons rate it below the AD8620. Those are forum opinions, not measurements.
Supply current is fairly high for a 5 V part (3.7 mA per amp typ), which matters for battery life in portable builds.

silicon_changes.when: PCN 23_0068 Rev. - published 8 May 2023, effective 10 Aug 2023; Rev. A published 6 Feb 2024 (models added), effective 10 May 2024
silicon_changes.identification: Not visible from the part marking. Wafer-fab origin can be traced only through ADI lot or date-code records. Parts made after Aug 2023 may come from TSMC or ADI Limerick wafers.
silicon_changes.summary: ADI added ADI Limerick (ADLK) as an alternate wafer fab to TSMC Fab 9, Fab 2A and Fab 2B for its 0.6 µm CMOS amplifier products. For a limited number of parts, wafer diameter also changed from 6 to 8 inches. ADI states no impact to fit, form, function or reliability, and has published qualification reports. Whether the AD8655 is listed was not confirmed.

silicon_changes.verification: A search confirmed the PCN scope (ADLK as an alternate to TSMC Fab 9/2A/2B for 0.6 µm CMOS amplifiers, no fit/form/function impact) and found the Rev. - and Rev. claims_confirmed: Current ADI datasheet is Rev. E at analog.com (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8655_8656.pdf); copyright 2005–2013.
TME hosts an older Rev. B copy of AD8655_8656.pdf (https://www.tme.eu/Document/97e591a5710fdf5735cb53b51b664371/AD8655_8656.pdf).

Specs: 2.7 nV/√Hz at 10 kHz, 250 µV max Vos over VCM, 0.4/2.3 µV/°C drift, 28 MHz bandwidth, 2.7–5.5 V, −40 to +125 °C, MSOP/SOIC (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8655_8656.pdf).

Specs: slew rate 11 V/µs (RL = 10 kΩ); supply current 3.7 mA typ / 4.5 mA max per amp; THD+N 0.0007% (G = 1, RL = 1 kΩ, 1 kHz, 2 V p-p); 220 mA output current (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8655_8656.pdf).
ADI describes the parts as the 'industry's lowest noise precision CMOS amplifiers' using DigiTrim (https://www.analog.com/en/products/ad8656.html).

PCN 23_0068: ADLK added as alternate wafer fab to TSMC Fab 9/2A/2B for 0.6 µm CMOS amps, 6-to-8-inch wafers for some parts, no fit/form/function impact. Rev - published 8 May 2023, effective 10 Aug 2023, includes the AD8656. Rev A published 6 Feb 2024, effective 10 May 2024 (https://www.analog.com/media/en/PCN/ADI_PCN_23_0068_Rev_A_Form.pdf, https://www.mouser.com/PCN/ADI_PCN_23_0068_Rev._A.pdf).
PCN 07_0024 Rev. E lists the AD8655 and AD8656 among affected products (https://www.analog.com/media/en/pcn/ADI_PCN_07_0024_Rev_E_Form.pdf).

revision_chain_notes:
Analog Devices is the only vendor. No second source, acquirer re-issue or TI/National/other edition exists for the AD8655/AD8656. The ADI datasheet file is AD8655_8656 ('Low Noise, Precision CMOS Amplifier Data Sheet AD8655/AD8656').

What is known, oldest to newest:
- Rev. 0 (original release, c. 2005, implied by the copyright 2005 on Rev. E): MISSING. No copy found.
- Rev. A: MISSING. No copy or date found.
- Rev. B: the TME copy is already listed. Its date is still not confirmed.
- Rev. C: MISSING.
- Rev. D: MISSING.
- Rev. E (c. 2013, copyright 2005–2013): the analog.com copy and the RadioLocman di=35348 copy are already listed. It is the current revision.

Four search queries using revision-history phrases ('Rev. D to Rev. E', 'Rev. C to Rev. D', 'Rev. 0 to Rev. A') and distributor/mirror terms found no snippet showing the Rev. 0, A, C or D headers, dates or change lists. The revision-history table in the current analog.com Rev. E PDF (not fetched, per tool rules) is the best place to recover the dates and changes for Rev. 0 through Rev. E.

New copies with the revision not shown, which may hold missing revisions:
- RadioLocman data.html?di=350009, a separate ID from the Rev. E entry.
- Scribd 94453684 'AD8655-6'. Its low ID suggests an upload around 2012, before Rev. E, so it may hold Rev. C or D. This is an inference and is not verified.
- datasheetspdf.com, DataSheetAll and ICDICTIONARY pages.
- Farnell 2250832.pdf. It is not confirmed to be this part.

Silicon-change evidence: PCN 23_0068 Rev. - (DigiKey copy) and Rev. A (Mouser copy) record the TSMC to ADI Limerick fab move (2023–2024). No datasheet revision after Rev. E has been seen to go with it.
